lines: -Before executing a migration operation, one of its precheck steps (a query expected to return true) did not hold: the database is not in the state the operation requires, so the apply stops and rolls back. When the step checks that a column becoming required has a value in every row (Postgres `SET NOT NULL`, or adding a required column for an empty table only), the runner counts the rows without one, here and for every other such column of the same migration (`rowsWithoutValue`), and the summary names the count, such as `3 rows of "Item" hold NULL in "note", so it cannot become required.` or `"User" has 2 rows, so the new required column "code" cannot be added: it can be added to an empty table only.` `db update` advises setting the values, keeping the field optional, or `migration plan --backfill <field>` for every field of the plan that needs it (with `--from <hash>` only when a migration on disk ends at the contract the database's marker names; otherwise the command has no `--from` and starts from the `db` ref); `db migrate` advises setting the values and re-running, keeping the field optional (make it optional in the contract again and plan the failed migration again), or deleting the failed migration's directory (after copying any code written in its `migration.ts`) and planning it again with the statements it was planned with and the printed `--backfill` flags (the printed command keeps the migration's name with `--name`, and every path the advice names is relative to the directory the command ran from, and every command it prints repeats the `--config` the command was given, so each runs as printed); `db init` advises initializing with the field optional, and then `db update`. No command offers a default: one value in every row breaks a unique or key field, and a default does not fill rows that hold NULL. Every piece of this advice that plans a migration says to fill in the `migration.ts` it writes, run that file with the `node` command `migration plan` prints, and only then apply it with `db migrate`: until the file runs, its `ops.json` holds no operations. When no other explanation applies, the `why` names the check and what its failure says of the database, such as `Before operation … runs, it checks: …. That check failed: the database already has ….` Payload: `failedCheck` (`operationId`, `phase`, `description`), and `rowsWithoutValue` when the runner counted rows (on SQLite, `failedTypeChange` when the check is a retyped column's). On MongoDB, where operations are not wrapped in a transaction, the operations before it stay applied, and a re-run skips them. A field rename (`renameField`) stops here when documents already hold the new name as well as the old one: the message names the collection, gives the `mongosh` query that finds those documents, and says to fix them and run the command again. A collection rename (`renameCollection`) stops here when the new collection already exists: the message names both collections, says nothing was renamed, and says to drop the new collection, or, when an earlier operation of the same migration created it, to make the rename the first operation of its `migration.ts`. Payload on MongoDB: `operationId`, `name` (a field rename only).
+A check an operation runs before it changes anything did not hold, so the apply stops. Postgres and SQLite roll back; on MongoDB the operations before it stay applied, and a re-run skips them.
+The `why` names the operation and the check: `Before operation … runs, it checks: …. That check failed on this database.`
+**A column becoming required has rows without a value.** The runner counts them (`rowsWithoutValue`), for example `3 rows of "Item" hold NULL in "note", so it cannot become required.` The advice:
+- `db update`: set the values, keep the field optional, or plan it with `migration plan --backfill <field>`.
+- `db migrate`: set the values and re-run, keep the field optional, or plan the failed migration again with the printed `--backfill` flags.
+- `db init`: initialize with the field optional, then run `db update`.

+No command offers a default: one value in every row breaks a unique field, and a default does not fill rows that hold NULL. A planned migration must have its `migration.ts` run with `node` before `db migrate` applies it.

+**MongoDB renames.** A field rename stops when documents already hold the new name; the message gives the `mongosh` query that finds them. A collection rename stops when the new collection exists; the message says to drop it, or to make the rename the first operation of its `migration.ts`.

+Payload: `failedCheck` (`operationId`, `phase`, `description`), and `rowsWithoutValue` or, on SQLite, `failedTypeChange` when the check found them. On MongoDB: `operationId`, and `name` for a field rename.
